blurb: Short-legged American cat breed, recognized by some registries and contested
description: The Munchkin is a US cat breed with very short legs caused by a dominant mutation; small to medium-sized, it is recognized by only some registries.
answer: The Munchkin is a domestic cat breed from the United States defined by very short legs, the result of a dominant chondrodysplasia mutation. It is a small to medium-sized cat of moderate build, and it is recognized by TICA and some other registries while others, including FIFe, the GCCF and the CFA, refuse it on welfare grounds.

body: Short-legged cats were documented from the 1940s, including a British veterinary report in 1944. Today's breed descends from Blackberry, a pregnant cat found in Rayville, Louisiana, in 1983 by music teacher Sandra Hochenedel, and her short-legged son Toulouse. The breed was shown to the public at a TICA show in 1991 and entered TICA's new breed program in 1994 amid much controversy, with full recognition in 1997. The name comes from the Munchkins of The Wonderful Wizard of Oz. Because of welfare concerns, breeding of dwarf cats such as the Munchkin is prohibited in several countries and territories.

Apart from its legs, the Munchkin resembles an ordinary domestic cat, since outcrossing to non-pedigree cats is allowed. It is small to medium-sized with a moderate body; males typically weigh about 2.7 to 4.1 kg and females about 1.8 to 3.6 kg. The hind legs can be slightly longer than the front, giving a slight rise toward the rump. All colors and patterns occur, in a medium-plush short coat or a semi-long silky longhair variety.
The source material says little about the Munchkin's personality beyond noting that it has characteristics similar to ordinary domestic cats. Individual temperament varies.

Sources disagree on mobility: some state the short legs do not interfere with running and leaping, while others say jumping ability is limited. Regular veterinary check-ups are advisable given the health concerns raised about the breed.

The short legs result from a chondrodysplasia mutation, and only cats carrying one copy are viable. Conditions reported in the breed include lordosis, pectus excavatum (hollowed chest) and a higher risk of severe osteoarthritis than other breeds. These health concerns are the reason many registries refuse to recognize the breed.

faq.q: Why do Munchkin cats have short legs?
faq.a: Their short legs are caused by an autosomal dominant chondrodysplasia mutation; kittens inheriting two copies are not viable.

faq.q: Is the Munchkin recognized by the FIFe or CFA?
faq.a: No. FIFe, the GCCF and the CFA do not recognize the Munchkin; TICA, the WCF and a few other registries do.
Sources differ: some say the short legs do not affect running and leaping, while others say jumping is limited.
